findings.finding: [frontend] GET /users/me/saved is correctly scoped to req.user!.id with no path/body-supplied user ID, so there is no IDOR risk of reading another user's saved-listing rows.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts: prisma.savedListing.findMany({ where: { userId: req.user!.id, listing: { status: { not: ListingStatus.REMOVED } } }, ... }) behind authenticate middleware.

findings.finding: [frontend] POST /listings/:id/save (untouched by this change) remains correctly scoped via the userId_listingId compound unique key, UUID-validates the :id param, requires authentication, and is rate-limited — verified this was not weakened.

[frontend] The REMOVED-listing filter added to GET /users/me/saved is a legitimate data-exposure fix (a user should not see a soft-deleted/removed listing surfaced as if still live) and is additive-only, consistent with the exclusion pattern already used in GET /listings and GET /listings/:id.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts diff adds listing: { status: { not: ListingStatus.REMOVED } } to the where clause.

findings.finding: [frontend] The user relation added to the saved-listings include only selects safe public fields (id, name, avatarUrl), matching the existing safe-field select pattern used elsewhere for listing owners — no email/phone/passwordHash exposure.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts: user: { select: { id: true, name: true, avatarUrl: true } }.

findings.finding: [frontend] /saved page auth gating reuses the exact pattern from /post (useIsAuthenticated + AuthModal auto-open + redirect home on close), not a new/weaker pattern, and does not attempt to fetch saved data before auth is confirmed.
findings.evidence: rentals/frontend/src/app/saved/page.tsx: useEffect only calls fetchSaved() when isAuth is true, otherwise opens AuthModal.

findings.finding: [frontend] No new dependencies, no raw SQL, no changes to messaging/admin routes, no schema migration — scope matches the task boundary.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat shows only rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts and rentals/frontend/src/components/listings/ListingCard.tsx changed (plus new saved/page.tsx and generated build artifacts).

findings.finding: [backend] GET /users/me/saved and POST /listings/:id/save both scope every Prisma query/mutation to req.user!.id via the (userId, listingId) compound unique key — verified no listingId-only or client-supplied userId lookup path exists, so a user cannot read or affect another user's saved-listing rows.
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/listings.ts:287-307 uses userId_listingId: { userId: req.user!.id, listingId: req.params.id } for both the existence check and delete; rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts:97 scopes findMany to userId: req.user!.id.

findings.finding: [backend] The only diff in this worktree (GET /users/me/saved) adds a status:ACTIVE filter and fixes response shape (amenities flattened to string[], isSaved:true added) to match what ListingCard expects. This is additive, non-schema-breaking, and closes a real de-listed-content exposure gap (a saved listing that was later soft-removed or deactivated would otherwise still be returned).
findings.evidence: rentals/backend/src/routes/users.ts diff: where now includes listing: { status: ListingStatus.ACTIVE }, matching the same exclusion already applied in GET /listings.

findings.finding: [backend] No schema.prisma change was made; SavedListing retains its @@unique([userId, listingId]) constraint and onDelete: Cascade on both userId and listingId relations, so duplicate saves are DB-enforced and hard-deleted listings cascade-clean orphaned SavedListing rows automatically.
